tasks.short: Explain techniques and safety procedures and demonstrate equipment to participants, prepare safety instruction cards, and record that participants received the safety instruction.

steps.what: Recreation worker explains principles, techniques and safety procedures and demonstrates use of equipment
Recreation worker prepares safety instruction cards
Recreation worker records on a paper list that participants received the safety instruction

tasks.design: Safety instruction cards per activity are kept in a shared library ({DOCS}) so workers print or show them instead of making their own. The booking system's participant list ({OTHER}) has a tick box for safety instruction received, replacing the paper list. Explaining and demonstrating stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each worker made own cards and kept paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared libraries and booking lists with tick boxes are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Participants do not read safety cards.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the participant who did not understand the instruction.

reach.learn: Whether safety instruction is recorded for every participant.

evidence.claim: Shared libraries and booking lists with tick boxes are standard tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the activity session to instruction recorded; activity design is outside.
Input contract: cards kept by the activity manager; fallback is own cards and paper lists.
Explaining and demonstrating do not change.
research_questions: Is safety instruction recorded for every participant?

incremental.description: Recreation worker suggests updates to shared cards.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few activities with equipment; high: many sessions with safety instruction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the special activity or event, handle participant registrations, check the programme and participant information, send the information to participants, and direct the event on the day.

steps.what: Recreation worker plans the special activity or event
Recreation worker handles participant registrations by phone and e-mail
Recreation worker checks the programme and participant information
Recreation worker e-mails the event information to participants
Recreation worker directs the special activity or event, such as aquatics or performing arts

tasks.design: Events start from a checklist template per event type ({DOCS}) with staffing, equipment and safety items. Participants register online in the booking system ({OTHER}), which keeps the list and capacity, instead of the worker taking calls and e-mails. Once the worker has checked the programme and list, the information goes to all participants from the booking system. Directing the event stays with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were made from scratch and registrations taken by phone and e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking systems take online registrations and send participant messages.
tasks.still_hard: Weather and late changes upset plans.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a group of nervous children calm before a show.

reach.learn: Whether more people register in time.

evidence.claim: Booking systems take online registrations, track capacity and message participants.

assumptions: Boundary: from the event request to the event held; event budgets are outside.
Input contract: templates kept by the team; fallback is phone and e-mail registration.
Participants register online in about the time a call took; a little participant time is priced.
Directing the event does not change.

incremental.description: Recreation worker sets up each event in the booking system.

approvals.approved_version: The programme and participant information as checked by the worker in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small events with few participants; high: large events with many registrations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make the duty roster, assign duties at the start of the day, train new staff, supervise staff during activities, and handle shift swaps.

steps.what: Recreation worker makes the duty roster in a spreadsheet
Recreation worker assigns work duties at the start of the day
Recreation worker trains new staff members
Recreation worker supervises personnel during activities
Recreation worker handles shift swap requests by message

tasks.design: Staff enter availability in a scheduling app ({CALENDAR}) that builds the roster within rules for skills, contract hours and rest times, and swaps are requested and approved in the same app. New staff take the theory of safety and procedures as online modules ({LMS}) before their first shift, so in-person training covers practice. Assigning duties and supervising stay with the worker; the app does not allocate shifts by behaviour or rate staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rosters were built in spreadsheets, swaps went through message groups and all training was in person.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling apps handle availability and swaps; learning systems deliver short modules.
tasks.still_hard: Seasonal staff join at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Matching a quiet new staff member with a patient colleague.

evidence.claim: Scheduling apps build rosters from availability and handle swaps; learning systems deliver short modules.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff availability to swaps handled; hiring is outside.
Input contract: availability from staff; modules from the employer; fallback is spreadsheets and in-person training.
Assigning and supervising do not change.
Staff enter availability in about the time a message took.

incremental.description: Recreation worker keeps roster rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small stable team; high: many seasonal staff.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect recreation areas and facilities, collect participant feedback, tally attendance and feedback, judge whether services produce the desired results, write the evaluation note, and send it to the manager.

steps.what: Recreation worker evaluates recreation areas and facilities on site
Recreation worker collects participant feedback on paper forms
Recreation worker tallies attendance and feedback in a spreadsheet
Recreation worker judges whether services are producing desired results
Recreation worker writes the evaluation note
Recreation worker e-mails the note to the manager

tasks.design: Participants get a short online survey by QR code or after-visit e-mail from the booking system ({OTHER}) instead of paper forms, and a dashboard ({BI}) shows attendance and survey results per activity. The evaluation note uses a template with the dashboard figures. Inspecting areas and judging results stay with the worker. Once written, the note goes to the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback was on paper and attendance tallied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking systems send surveys and feed dashboards.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why a well-attended activity still disappoints people.
tasks.altitude: The worker reads figures instead of tallying them.

evidence.claim: Booking systems can send surveys and feed attendance dashboards.

assumptions: Boundary: from the evaluation period to the note sent; budget decisions are outside.
Input contract: attendance in the booking system; fallback is paper forms and tallies.
Participants fill the online survey in about the time a paper form took; no added participant time.
Inspecting and judging do not change.
research_questions: Does the survey response rate hold up online?

incremental.description: Recreation worker sets up surveys per activity.

approvals.approved_version: The note as written by the worker in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few activities; high: many activities with regular surveys.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The recreation worker keeps instructing, directing events, supervising staff and judging services; paper lists, spreadsheet rosters and hand tallies shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the booking and scheduling systems
role.ambitious_version: A worker with more time with participants.
